bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to commerce; regulating homeowner's insurance advertisements; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 72A.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[72A.329] HOMEOWNER'S INSURANCE ADVERTISING.

An insurance company licensed to do business in Minnesota that offers homeowner's insurance coverage, as defined by section 65A.27, must include the following information in print, televised, electronic, and radio advertisements:

(1) the total amount the insurance company spent on advertising and marketing during the previous calendar year; and

(2) if the insurance company is publicly traded, the increase or decrease in the insurance company's stock prices for the previous calendar year.
additions: An insurance company licensed to do business in Minnesota that offers homeowner's insurance coverage, as defined by section 65A.27, must include the following information in print, televised, electronic, and radio advertisements:
(1) the total amount the insurance company spent on advertising and marketing during the previous calendar year; and
(2) if the insurance company is publicly traded, the increase or decrease in the insurance company's stock prices for the previous calendar year.
